flagged.evidence: The link definition permits k components for k in N, and N includes 0, so the empty link has an empty regular projection P. The connected-graph definition states: “A graph is connected when its vertex set is nonempty and every two vertices are reachable from one another. Thus the null graph is not connected.” Hence P is disconnected, but it has no points on either side of any curve, contrary to the Statement. Require P to be nonempty.

The empty link is allowed and its empty regular projection is the null graph, which is disconnected under the library’s graph convention. But the split-link definition requires a sphere whose two complementary components each contain link points; the empty link has none. Thus the Statement’s hypothesis holds while its conclusion does not. Require a nonempty diagram/link.

The Statement introduces “K a nonempty oriented link,” then refers to “a regular diagram D” in defining f_K, without saying D represents K. As written, K could be the trefoil while D is a crossing-free unknot diagram, giving f_K=1; the in-scope worked example computes the trefoil polynomial as t+t^3-t^4. The later proof’s choice of a braid closure for K does not supply the missing relation in the Statement.
